## Research Experience

### [Functional Multi-Task Learning with Similar Representations](posts/functional-mtl/)

*Sept. 2024–Present*

**Abstract.** We study scalar-on-multiple-function regression with several related regression tasks whose underlying representations may not be identical. Within each informative task, the vector of slope functions is assumed to admit a low-dimensional representation, with task-specific representation subspaces remaining close to a common subspace, while a fraction of tasks may be unrelated. We develop two estimation procedures based on penalized empirical risk minimization and robust spectral aggregation, respectively. Both procedures learn representations across tasks and then perform task-specific refitting. The refitting step measures deviations in a prediction–roughness geometry that reflects the functional design and smoothness regularization. We establish upper bounds on prediction error that characterize when cross-task information improves estimation and how task-specific refitting guards against negative transfer. Simulation studies evaluate the finite-sample performance of the proposed methods, followed by an application to multi-site air-quality data.

**Status.** Manuscript submitted.

### Microsimulation and Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of AI-Assisted HPB Cancer Screening

*Dec. 2024– May. 2026*

**Research Summary.** Developed an individual-level lifecycle microsimulation model to evaluate the long-term cost-effectiveness of the HOPE three-tier AI-assisted cancer screening strategy compared with standard clinical care. The model integrates disease progression, repeated screening, cancer detection, treatment, mortality, healthcare costs, and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs). Base-case, probabilistic, and one-way sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess cost-effectiveness and quantify uncertainty in model assumptions and input parameters.

**Role.** Research Collaborator.

**Status.** Manuscript in preparation.
